policy.sourceRule: Use only official vendor documentation for compatibility claims. If the official docs do not document a capability, record not documented or unknown.
policy.nonVendorRule: A small number of non-vendor runtimes (e.g. gajae-code, a community/MIT project) are tracked from their own project README rather than vendor docs. They must be explicitly flagged as community/non-vendor in the docs, held to the same not-documented discipline, and never presented as official vendor guarantees.
policy.mainBranchRule: Daily automation must create a PR; it must not push directly to main.

sources.notes: NON-VENDOR community project (MIT, beta) by Yeachan-Heo; this README is the only source, not vendor docs. Flagged the same way Kuma Studio is. Verified 2026-07-07. A coding-agent harness (binary `gjc`) that runs adjacent to other CLIs; install with `bun install -g gajae-code` (scoped `@gajae-code/coding-agent`). Interactive `gjc` / `gjc --tmux` / `gjc --tmux --worktree <branch>`; headless `gjc --mode rpc` (no JSON/output-format flag). Skills are the only documented extension surface: SKILL.md-format bundled skills installed by `gjc setup defaults` into the user `.gjc` directory (2026-07-05: the exact `~/.gjc/skills/` path is no longer literally stated in the README), listed/read with `gjc skills list` / `gjc skills read <name>`, invoked as `/skill:<name>` (colon form), defaults deep-interview/ralplan/ultragoal/team. Hooks, plugins, session-id resume, and project-instruction-file loading are all NOT documented (re-confirmed by grep). User config `~/.gjc/config.yml`; per-project state `.gjc/`. New README content (0.6-0.7, outside claim scope): `gjc rlm` research/REPL mode, notifications SDK + `gjc daemon` Telegram reference daemon, image input, standalone RPC/ACP/Bridge external-control surfaces (2026-07-07: 'MCP' no longer appears in the README — the external-control pointer names RPC, ACP, and Bridge/HTTPS via docs/external-control-readiness.md), an experimental opt-in `computer-use` desktop-control tool surface (2026-07-07: the README no longer states any 0.x version marker in its text, so the earlier 0.6.0 tie is gone), and a four-role bundled agent table (executor/architect/planner/critic).
